facts.raw_span: 20-year history of progressive ataxia
8-month history of 'spasms' in his throat
difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Hypometric saccades
Truncal and limb ataxia
Decreased vibratory sense with inability to ambulate
Bradykinesia and mild rigidity
Palatal myoclonus at a frequency of 1-2 Hz
Patient was unable to stop myoclonus of the palate with voluntary use of the palatal musculature
No clicking was noted by patient or examiners
Results of testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 were normal
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

concepts.why: The patient has a 20-year history of progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, which are characteristic of spinocerebellar ataxia.
The patient has bradykinesia, rigidity, and palatal myoclonus, which are symptoms of multiple system atrophy, and also has severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy.
The patient has hypometric saccades, bradykinesia, and rigidity, which are characteristic of progressive supranuclear palsy, and also has severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy.
The patient has a 20-year history of progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, which are characteristic of olivopontocerebellar atrophy.
The patient has bradykinesia, rigidity, and palatal myoclonus, which are symptoms of corticobasal degeneration, and also has severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy.
The patient has a 20-year history of progressive ataxia, hypometric saccades, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, which are characteristic of ataxia with oculomotor apraxia.
It explains the patient's inability to stop myoclonus of the palate with voluntary use of the palatal musculature.
It explains the patient's decreased vibratory sense with inability to ambulate.
